charts.title: How an old stated uncertainty is scored against the value printed later.
charts.takeaway: Each later value is placed inside or outside the earlier edition's interval; the 1 sigma interval covers about as often as it should, and covering 95.45 percent takes 3.8 to 4.9 sigma where a normal error needs 2.
charts.n: 227 PDG values that moved, 2,213 AME values, 211 CODATA values, 544 Hubble constant values

steps.label: Tables of record, several editions
steps.detail: PDG particle properties 2010 to 2025, AME atomic masses 2003 to 2020, CODATA constants 2002 to 2022, and 544 published Hubble constant values.

steps.label: Shift in units of the old sigma
steps.detail: The later value minus the earlier value, divided by the earlier sigma (the stated standard uncertainty printed beside a value).

steps.label: Coverage and needed multiple
steps.detail: Coverage is the share of shifts inside 1 or 2 sigma. A normal error gives 0.6827 and 0.9545. The needed multiple is how many sigma it takes to reach those shares.

steps.label: Planted: recovered 2.405
steps.detail: A made-up world with stated errors at half the true error. The true multiple is 2.394.

steps.label: Control: honest normal world
steps.detail: Standard normal shifts at the PDG sample size, 500 draws. Shortfall from 0.6827: mean 0.0005, 95th percentile 0.040.

steps.label: 3.8 to 4.9 sigma for 95.45 percent
steps.detail: 1 sigma coverage: PDG 0.68, AME 0.66. The stated sigma is about right in the middle and too small in the tails.

charts.title: How often the earlier stated interval held the later value.
charts.takeaway: At 1 sigma, PDG (0.68) and AME (0.66) sit near the nominal 0.6827; at 2 sigma both fall short of 0.9545 (0.85 and 0.82), and early Hubble constant values cover only 0.35 at 1 sigma.
charts.units: share of later values inside the earlier interval, 0 to 1, where sigma (the stated standard uncertainty printed beside a value) sets the interval; a share below the dashed nominal line means the stated uncertainty was too small

charts.title: How many stated sigma it takes to cover 95.45 percent of later values.
charts.takeaway: A normal error needs 2; the tables needed 3.8 (PDG), 4.0 (AME) and 4.9 (CODATA), so the far ends of the stated uncertainty are about half as wide as they should be.
charts.units: needed multiple: the number of stated sigma that holds 95.45 percent of the later values; a normal error needs 2, and a larger number means heavier tails

charts.title: The tail shape of the shifts, as a fitted Student t.
charts.takeaway: Fitted nu is 1.67 for PDG, 1.22 for AME and 2.17 for CODATA, all close to 1, the Cauchy shape, whose large misses are common.
charts.units: nu: the degrees of freedom of a Student t curve fitted to the nonzero shifts. A smaller nu means heavier tails; 1 is the Cauchy shape and a normal curve is the limit of very large nu
charts.n: nonzero shifts among 347 PDG, 2,213 AME and 211 CODATA values
